items.followUp: Name the two common types of network connection and give one example of each.

rubric.why: Identifies the two basic connection types.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying both types.

rubric.why: Shows the distinction between the two types.
rubric.description: Gives suitable examples or clearly distinguishes wired from wireless.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for suitable examples or a clear distinction.

modelAnswer: Network connections are of two types: wired and wireless.
A wired connection uses a cable; a wireless connection can use Wi-Fi.

items.followUp: What does a web browser send to a web server when requesting a web page?

rubric.why: Identifies the two ends of the communication.
rubric.description: States that a client communicates with a server over the Internet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying client and server communication.

rubric.why: Names a way or protocol used to reach the server.
rubric.description: Mentions the server's IP address/domain name or TCP/IP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct addressing method or protocol.

modelAnswer: A client connects to a server over the Internet using the TCP/IP protocol.
The client sends a request to the server’s IP address (or its domain name, which resolves to an IP address).

items.followUp: Write HTML code to display the text “Computer” in a font size of 18 pixels.

rubric.why: Checks that the requested text appears in the HTML element.
rubric.description: Includes the text Punjab in the code.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly including Punjab.

rubric.why: Checks that the requested size is specified.
rubric.description: Sets the text size to 24, preferably as 24px.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct size specification.

items.followUp: Write the names of the three types of lists used in HTML.

rubric.why: Recognizes the two common list types.
Recognizes the third HTML list type.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the description/definition list.

modelAnswer: HTML has three types of lists: ordered lists, unordered lists, and description (definition) lists.

items.followUp: What does the colspan attribute do in an HTML table?

rubric.why: Identifies the attribute’s direction of effect.
rubric.description: States that rowspan concerns table rows.

rubric.why: Explains what the attribute does to a cell.
rubric.description: States that a cell extends across or occupies multiple rows.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the cell spans more than one row.

modelAnswer: The rowspan attribute specifies how many rows a table cell should span.
It allows a cell to extend vertically across multiple rows.

items.followUp: Define a row in an HTML table.

rubric.description: States that a table is an HTML structure or arrangement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a table as a structure or arrangement.

rubric.why: Describes the table’s contents or layout.
rubric.description: States that a table arranges data in rows and columns.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning data arranged in rows and columns.

modelAnswer: A table is an arrangement of data in rows and columns.
In HTML, a table is made up of rows and cells.

rubric.description: Explains that integrity protects the accuracy and completeness of data from unauthorized alteration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing data accuracy or protection from unauthorized changes.

rubric.description: Explains that confidentiality prevents information from being disclosed to unauthorized people.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing restricted access or disclosure.

modelAnswer: Integrity means ensuring that data remains accurate and complete and is not changed without authorization.
Confidentiality means keeping information private and preventing its disclosure to unauthorized people.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of a username in addition to a password?

rubric.description: States that a password protects a user account or system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning protection of an account or system.

rubric.why: Explains how the password provides protection.
rubric.description: States that a password helps verify an authorized user or prevent unauthorized access.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining its access-control purpose.

modelAnswer: A password protects a user account or computer system from unauthorized access.
It helps verify that the person trying to access it is an authorized user.
